subject: Queue pile-up / reserved throughput gap — QuantaPay impact
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@quantapay.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@quantapay.com>, ops@quantapay.com
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden queue pile-up — impacting reconciliation jobs

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a huge backlog on our reconciliation batch starting ~08:45 PDT — token queue depth jumped, tail latency spiked to >12s and a handful of requests returned 5xx. This is happening against our reserved capacity (QTP-4521). Impact: settlement runs delayed, downstream accounting alerts firing.

I attached a snapshot of the token queue and a screenshot of GPU util. Can your team confirm whether this is a capacity throttling / scheduler regression on your side or something from our side? We’re on a tight close window — need to understand fallback options and any compensation path.

Appreciate fast response.

— Samir
Head of Platform, QuantaPay

Attachments: quantapay_token_queue_snapshot_0531.json, nv-gpu-util-0531.png

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Samir Shah <samir@quantapay.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@quantapay.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:28:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden queue pile-up — impacting reconciliation jobs

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I’m escalating immediately. Quick summary for transparency: QuantaPay reserved pool (QTP-4521) is showing a sustained queue depth increase in the 08:40–09:10 window with correlated token-token latency and increased 5xx rate. We are treating this as a reserved-capacity throughput shortfall until proven otherwise.

Next steps we’re kicking off now:
- David: can you confirm if the autoscaling policy attempted any burst allocations and whether those were denied due to headroom exhaustion?
- Vivek: please start a live metrics snapshot and check routing/fallback logs for the tenant.
- Samir: if you have any recent traffic pattern changes (batch size, concurrency, model variant) please paste here — we’ll include that in the RCA.

We will keep you updated every 30 minutes until stabilized. If needed we’ll request burst authorization and open an exec bridge.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: david.kim@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@quantapay.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 10:05:17 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden queue pile-up — initial telemetry

Quick update (initial telemetry):
- Autoscaler: no burst allocation triggered for QTP-4521 between 08:30–09:15. Policy shows burst disabled for this tenant (reserved-only routing).
- GPU farm: several nearby pools at 92–97% util, limited spare headroom in region-us-west-2.
- Scheduler logs: observed increased scheduling latency (median scheduling microseconds -> 3x) and a small uptick in KV-cache eviction activity for model kvs.
- Error pattern: 82% of 5xx are timeouts from worker-side forwarder (503-style). Not seeing model OOMs.

Attached: billing-usage-0530.csv for usage delta and a short snapshot of queue state (uploaded to Drive). My read: reserved throughput cap was exceeded during a short burst window and the tenant was not eligible for cross-pool overflow under current policy.

If we want to restore within the hour: two options — temporarily enable burst overflow (requires ops & billing approval) or initiate prioritized manual spill to a compatible dedicated variant (risk: slightly higher tail latency but avoids 5xx). Recommend we request a one-time burst authorization and prepare the spill plan in parallel.

— David
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: billing-usage-0530.csv, drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/quantapay/ops-logs/0531

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Samir Shah <samir@quantapay.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@quantapay.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, vivek_leadership@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden queue pile-up — executive escalation + remediation plan

Samir / Elena — status update and plan of record: we’ve confirmed the root cause is a short-lived reserved-capacity throughput shortfall combined with regional GPU headroom depletion. Important notes: this is NOT a model correctness issue; it's capacity routing/policy behavior during a high concurrency burst tied to your morning settlement window.

Immediate remediation we’re executing now (ETA 20–30m):
1) Burst authorization requested and approved by ops on-call — we are enabling overflow to compatible pools in us-west-2 for a one-hour window.
2) We will temporarily divert low-priority non-reconciliation traffic off your reserved pool (we will not touch production reconciliation traffic).
3) Engineering will open a prioritized spill to a quantized variant to reduce per-token runtime cost and free headroom.
4) We will issue a one-time invoice credit for the service degradation (billing will follow up with the exact amount).

Follow-ups (owners and ETA):
- David: full RCA draft in 48 hours (involving scheduler patch timeline).
- Vivek: recommend persistent policy change: allow conditional overflow for reserved tenants during critical windows (proposal within 72 hours).
- Marissa (me): coordinate customer comms and finalize credit.

Samir — I’ll set a 30-min bridge and include ops and a product policy lead so we can align on both immediate lift and policy changes to prevent recurrence. Appreciate your patience — we own the remediation.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Forwarded-For-Execs: attaching the three artifacts Samir sent and David's billing snapshot for leadership visibility.

Attachments: quantapay_token_queue_snapshot_0531.json, nv-gpu-util-0531.png, billing-usage-0530.csv
